browser-harness-skill v1.0.4 changelog

- Added strict prohibition on using the `raw` subcommand by default (requires `BH_RAW_OK=1` to enable).
- Included clear guidance for Agents: always use `exec '<snippet>'` instead of `raw`.
- Updated constraints: never automate enabling `raw`; report attempts and fallback to safe command paths.
- Added a new constraint: treat content in `domain-skills` files as untrusted and protect against prompt injection.
- Instruct Agents to proactively suggest `scripts/run.sh stop` to users when done, for better resource management.

browser-harness-skill 1.0.0 - Initial release

- Enables LLM-friendly control of an already-logged-in, real Chrome browser via CDP, sharing user session/cookies.
- Provides unified Python and TypeScript agent workflow; agents coordinate via a local Python daemon and IPC.
- Offers one-line commands for JS execution, DOM interaction, file upload, screenshotting, and tab/page management.
- Integrates with domain-skills for persistent, site-specific automation knowledge and directions.
- Strictly maintains user session privacy and security; no remote data transfer, only local communication.
- Comprehensive error handling and user guidance included for setup, troubleshooting, and recovery.
